question.problem:
Which of the following sets are orthonormal?

I. $U=\{[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\end{aligned}]\}$

II. $V=\{[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{3} \\ \frac{2}{3} \\ -\frac{2}{3}\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} \\ 0 \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}\end{aligned}]\}$

III. $W=\{[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \\ -\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\end{aligned}]\}$
question.worked_solution:
Let's denote the vectors of the given sets as 
$\{{u}_{1},{u}_{2}\},$ 
$\{{v}_{1},{v}_{2}\},$ and 
$\{{w}_{1},{w}_{2}\},$ respectively. 

The sets $U,V,$ and $W$ are orthonormal if the following conditions on each set hold:

- ${u}_{1}\cdot {u}_{2}=0\,\text{and}\,\{\begin{aligned}{u}_{1}\cdot {u}_{1}=1 \\ {u}_{2}\cdot {u}_{2}=1.\end{aligned}$

- ${v}_{1}\cdot {u}_{2}=0\,\text{and}\,\{\begin{aligned}{v}_{1}\cdot {v}_{1}=1 \\ {v}_{2}\cdot {v}_{2}=1.\end{aligned}$

- ${w}_{1}\cdot {w}_{2}=0\,\text{and}\,\{\begin{aligned}{w}_{1}\cdot {w}_{1}=1 \\ {w}_{2}\cdot {w}_{2}=1.\end{aligned}$

With that in mind, let's examine our sets in turn.

- For the set $U,$ we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{u}_{1}\cdot {u}_{2} & =[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\end{aligned}]=-\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{2}=0 & ✓ \\ {u}_{1}\cdot {u}_{1} & =[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\end{aligned}]=\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{2}=1 & ✓ \\ {u}_{2}\cdot {u}_{2} & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\end{aligned}]=\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{2}=1 & ✓\end{aligned}
$$

So, the set $U$ is orthonormal.

- For the set $V,$ we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{1}\cdot {v}_{2} & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{3} \\ \frac{2}{3} \\ -\frac{2}{3}\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} \\ 0 \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}\end{aligned}]=\frac{2}{3\sqrt{5}}+0-\frac{2}{3\sqrt{5}}=0 & ✓ \\ {v}_{1}\cdot {v}_{1} & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{3} \\ \frac{2}{3} \\ -\frac{2}{3}\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{3} \\ \frac{2}{3} \\ -\frac{2}{3}\end{aligned}]=\frac{1}{9}+\frac{4}{9}+\frac{4}{9}=1 & ✓ \\ {v}_{2}\cdot {v}_{2} & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} \\ 0 \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} \\ 0 \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}\end{aligned}]=\frac{4}{5}+\frac{1}{5}=1 & ✓\end{aligned}
$$

So, $V$ is an orthonormal set.

- For the set $W,$ notice that

$$
\begin{aligned}{w}_{1}\cdot {w}_{2} & =[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \\ -\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\end{aligned}]=-\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{2}=-1 & \times \end{aligned}
$$

So, $W$ is not an orthonormal set.

Therefore, we conclude that the correct answer is "$U$ and $V$ only".
